text:
Ellen Park: Quick thought — we should decompose the console data path into a projection service + an auth-filter layer. Keeps denorm/caching separate from permission logic. Sketch below.

Praveen Singh: curious — what are the clear pros vs cons you see?

Ellen Park: Pros:
- clear cache boundaries (proj svc can return denormalized blobs optimized for UI)
- independent scaling for heavy read workloads
- easier MV/materialized view placement without RBAC complexity
- simpler perf optimizations (vectorized serialization, prefetch)

Zoe Martinez: Cons: extra network hop, more moving parts to test, increased surface for consistency bugs, and we need to be explicit about eventual consistency semantics.

Praveen Singh: Alternate is DB-level enforcement (Postgres RLS) — one hop, enforced close to the data. But RLS struggles at scale with large ACL tables and complex joins; also harder to cache safely.

Ellen Park: Agreed — RLS is attractive for correctness but makes pre-aggregation and cross-tenant queries painful. Our metrics folks also reported problems when trying to build real-time MVs when RLS predicates were complex.

Zoe Martinez: For caching: could projection svc return fully pre-filtered view for a given principal? e.g. `GET /v1/console/views/:id?principal=...` and projection returns denorm JSON keyed by principal?

Ellen Park: Yes — pattern would be: projection returns denormalized payloads (customer-centric), auth-filter is a thin policy layer that masks or rejects fields. Projection can be cached by customer+view, auth-filter uses a short-lived permission cache (redis) to short-circuit checks.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: canary perf run on staging tomorrow 07:00 UTC (tags: console-proj-poC).

Praveen Singh: Perf tradeoffs: extra hop looks like ~0.8–1.5ms p95 in our infra, but buys independent autoscaling and targeted caching. We need benchmark matrix: baseline (current), projection-only, projection+auth, db-rls. Also test under high ACL cardinality.

Zoe Martinez: Action items: 1) projection PoC (denorm schema + sample payloads), 2) perf harness + synthetic ACL generator, 3) infra SR for redis cluster + sizing, 4) update console SDK to accept masked payloads.

Ellen Park: I'll open an RFC PR with interface sketches, example request/response, and failure modes. Tagging @Praveen and @Zoe for review. ETA: EOD Friday.

Zoe Martinez: :thumbsup: Also define a cache key format early: `console:proj:<view_id>:<customer_id>:<version>` to avoid cache poisoning.

Praveen Singh: Add failure-mode rules to RFC: auth-filter fallback should default to safe-mask (hide sensitive fields) and surface a non-500 sentinel so UI can show partial data instead of a hard error. Include circuit-breaker behavior when auth svc is degraded.

Ellen Park: Perfect. I'll include perf targets and the benchmark plan in the RFC. Will post link here once it's up.
